title: Brute-force login attack from a single IP range
symptoms: Burst of 'Login failed for user admin from 175.45.176.23 port 51234': hundreds of events within 5 minutes. Source IPs geolocate to a high-risk country. Many different usernames are tried, like root, admin, test and deploy.
root_cause: An automated attacker is guessing passwords against the login endpoint, cycling through common usernames from a small block of IP addresses.
impact: Risk of account takeover if any password is weak. Extra load on the auth service; real users may be locked out by lockout rules.
fix_steps: Block the offending IP range at the firewall or WAF (e.g. 175.45.176.0/22).
Enable or tighten fail2ban / rate limiting on the login endpoint.
Check auth logs for any SUCCESSFUL login from the same range and force a password reset for those accounts.
Disable or rename default accounts such as admin, root and test.
prevention: Enforce MFA, rate-limit logins per IP and per user, geo-block countries you never serve, and alert on login bursts.
